comments.text: I am usually with my 14-year-old because we agree that having two sets of ears to hear what the doctor is telling us is better than just one. He knows I'm his advocate and usually wants me there, but occasionally has asked for privacy and I immediately leave.  I also feel that just giving him that option shows him I respect his growing autonomy and I have his wellbeing in mind.  Parents, I'd say that being willing to let these more private conversations happen is a green flag for the doctor - abusers are the ones who don't want their child alone with a care provider.  And are we not raising our kids to be autonomous adults?  While you're in the waiting room, they're learning to advocate for their own health care and that will be a very valuable skill for them to have.  It's hard to pull back on our parental instincts and we can torture ourselves while waiting, wondering if they're talking about us (even the best parents aren't perfect!), but just because it's hard, doesn't mean it's not the right thing to do
